reasons.specificity: It closely tracks Castoriadis’s distinct product/cost, firm-imputation, preference-formation, temporal, and globalization boundaries rather than offering a generic externalities critique.
reasons.anchoring: The quoted passages support nearly every interpretation, including regime-defined costs, fuzzy collective production, socially formed wants, provisional foreign-trade abstraction, and globally heterogeneous production conditions.
reasons.non_obviousness: It usefully distinguishes criticism of separability from rejection of all bounded models, and accounting exclusion from endorsement of a commensurating full-cost metric.
reasons.coherence: The prose, inclusion/exclusion map, alternative-boundary table, findings ledger, and counter-evidence consistently preserve the source’s qualifications and distinguish source claims from analyst proposals.
reasons.usefulness: The tables provide an accurate, text-open guide to how changing boundaries alters visible problems, while the open questions prevent the reframings from masquerading as operational solutions.
reasons.hallucination_risk: Claims are overwhelmingly source-supported, though references to labor as nationally constrained and to who bears adjustment costs extend slightly beyond what Castoriadis explicitly formulates.

score.one_line: A highly specific, well-anchored boundary reading whose main weakness is slight analytical extension in the globalization reframing and somewhat overstated claims of complete coverage.
